
```{r install-packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Install required packages (Run only ONCE)
install.packages("car")
install.packages("corrplot")
install.packages("leaps")
install.packages("MASS")
install.packages("ggplot2")
install.packages("Metrics")  # For RMSE, MAE calculation

# Load packages
library(car)
library(corrplot)
library(leaps)
library(MASS)
library(ggplot2)
library(Metrics)
```


```{r read-data}
# Read the cleaned dataset
df <- read.csv("D:/cleaned_student_data_final.csv")

# Confirm dataset loaded
cat("Rows    :", nrow(df), "\n")  # Expected: 49204
cat("Columns :", ncol(df), "\n")  # Expected: 18

head(df)
str(df)
```



```{r prepare-data}
# Select only variables needed for MLR
# Excluded:
# - student_id     : ID only, not a predictor
# - engagement_score: composite variable, highly correlated
#                    with study_hours_weekly (r=0.79)
#                    including both causes multicollinearity
# - gender, country, device_type : categorical — not in this MLR
# - dropout        : binary outcome, not a predictor

df_mlr <- df[, c("final_grade",
                  "age",
                  "internet_speed_mbps",
                  "study_hours_weekly",
                  "login_frequency_weekly",
                  "avg_session_duration_min",
                  "video_watch_time_min",
                  "assignments_submitted",
                  "forum_posts",
                  "quiz_attempts",
                  "avg_quiz_score",
                  "attendance_rate")]

cat("Variables selected:", ncol(df_mlr), "\n")
cat("Rows              :", nrow(df_mlr), "\n")
cat("Missing values    :", sum(is.na(df_mlr)), "\n")
```


```{r train-test-split}
# WHY: We split the dataset into training (80%) and testing (20%).
# Training data  → used to BUILD the model
# Testing data   → used to EVALUATE how well the model predicts
#                  on unseen data
# This checks whether our model generalizes well (not overfitted)

# Set seed for reproducibility — same split every time
set.seed(123)

# Create random 80% sample index
train_index <- sample(1:nrow(df_mlr),
                      size    = 0.8 * nrow(df_mlr),
                      replace = FALSE)

# Split into train and test
train_df <- df_mlr[train_index,  ]   # 80% for training
test_df  <- df_mlr[-train_index, ]   # 20% for testing

# Confirm split sizes
cat("Total rows      :", nrow(df_mlr), "\n")
cat("Training rows   :", nrow(train_df),
    "(", round(nrow(train_df)/nrow(df_mlr)*100, 1), "%)\n")
cat("Testing rows    :", nrow(test_df),
    "(", round(nrow(test_df)/nrow(df_mlr)*100, 1), "%)\n")
```



```{r correlation-analysis}
# WHY: We check correlations using TRAINING data only.
# This shows which variables are strongly related to final_grade
# and identifies potential multicollinearity between predictors.

# Calculate correlation matrix from training data
cor_matrix <- cor(train_df)

# Correlation with final_grade
cat("=== Correlation with final_grade ===\n")
print(sort(cor_matrix["final_grade", ], decreasing = TRUE))

# Visualize correlation heatmap
corrplot(cor_matrix,
         method      = "color",
         type        = "upper",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex  = 0.5,
         tl.cex      = 0.6,
         title       = "Correlation Matrix — Training Data",
         mar         = c(0,0,1,0))
```


```{r full-model}
# WHY: Build full model with ALL 11 predictors using training data.
# This is the baseline — we can see which variables are significant
# and which are not, BEFORE applying variable selection.

full_model <- lm(final_grade ~ age +
                               internet_speed_mbps +
                               study_hours_weekly +
                               login_frequency_weekly +
                               avg_session_duration_min +
                               video_watch_time_min +
                               assignments_submitted +
                               forum_posts +
                               quiz_attempts +
                               avg_quiz_score +
                               attendance_rate,
                 data = train_df)   # Use TRAINING data

full_summary <- summary(full_model)
full_summary

# Key metrics
cat("\n=== FULL MODEL METRICS ===\n")
cat("Multiple R²  :", round(full_summary$r.squared,     4), "\n")
cat("Adjusted R²  :", round(full_summary$adj.r.squared, 4), "\n")
cat("F-statistic  :", round(full_summary$fstatistic[1],  2), "\n")
cat("AIC          :", round(AIC(full_model),             2), "\n")
```



```{r vif-check}
# WHY: VIF detects multicollinearity among predictor variables.
# Multicollinearity means two or more predictors are highly correlated
# with each other — this makes coefficients unstable and unreliable.
#
# Decision Rule:
# VIF = 1        → No multicollinearity
# 1 < VIF < 5   → Acceptable
# 5 <= VIF < 10 → Concern
# VIF >= 10     → Serious problem

vif_values <- vif(full_model)

# VIF table
vif_table <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(vif_values),
  VIF      = round(vif_values, 4),
  Decision = ifelse(vif_values < 5,
                    "Acceptable",
                    ifelse(vif_values < 10,
                           "Concern",
                           "Serious Problem"))
)
print(vif_table)

# VIF bar plot
barplot(vif_values,
        main      = "VIF Values — Full Model",
        ylab      = "VIF",
        col       = ifelse(vif_values > 5, "red", "steelblue"),
        las       = 2,
        cex.names = 0.65)
abline(h = 5,  col = "orange", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
abline(h = 10, col = "red",    lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topright",
       legend = c("Threshold = 5", "Threshold = 10"),
       col    = c("orange","red"),
       lty = 2, lwd = 2)
```


```{r best-subset}
# WHY: Best Subset tries ALL possible variable combinations and
# picks the best model size based on Adjusted R², Cp, and BIC.
# Adjusted R² — maximize (higher = better fit)
# Cp          — minimize (lower = less bias)
# BIC         — minimize (lower = better balance of fit & simplicity)

model_best <- regsubsets(final_grade ~ age +
                                       internet_speed_mbps +
                                       study_hours_weekly +
                                       login_frequency_weekly +
                                       avg_session_duration_min +
                                       video_watch_time_min +
                                       assignments_submitted +
                                       forum_posts +
                                       quiz_attempts +
                                       avg_quiz_score +
                                       attendance_rate,
                         data  = train_df,
                         nvmax = 11)

best_summary <- summary(model_best)

# Criteria table
criteria_df <- data.frame(
  Num_Vars = 1:11,
  Adj_R2   = round(best_summary$adjr2, 4),
  Cp       = round(best_summary$cp,    4),
  BIC      = round(best_summary$bic,   4),
  RSS      = round(best_summary$rss,   2)
)
print(criteria_df)

# Best model by each criterion
cat("\nBest by Adjusted R²:", which.max(best_summary$adjr2), "variables\n")
cat("Best by Cp         :", which.min(best_summary$cp),    "variables\n")
cat("Best by BIC        :", which.min(best_summary$bic),   "variables\n")

# Plot criteria
par(mfrow = c(1,3))

plot(best_summary$adjr2, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Number of Variables", ylab = "Adjusted R²",
     main = "Best Subset: Adjusted R²")
points(which.max(best_summary$adjr2),
       max(best_summary$adjr2), col = "red", pch = 20, cex = 2)
abline(v = which.max(best_summary$adjr2), col = "red", lty = 2)

plot(best_summary$cp, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Number of Variables", ylab = "Cp",
     main = "Best Subset: Cp")
points(which.min(best_summary$cp),
       min(best_summary$cp), col = "red", pch = 20, cex = 2)
abline(v = which.min(best_summary$cp), col = "red", lty = 2)

plot(best_summary$bic, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "steelblue",
     xlab = "Number of Variables", ylab = "BIC",
     main = "Best Subset: BIC")
points(which.min(best_summary$bic),
       min(best_summary$bic), col = "red", pch = 20, cex = 2)
abline(v = which.min(best_summary$bic), col = "red", lty = 2)

par(mfrow = c(1,1))

# Variables in best BIC model
bic_best <- which.min(best_summary$bic)
cat("\nVariables in best BIC model (", bic_best, "vars):\n")
print(coef(model_best, bic_best))
```




```{r backward-elimination}
# WHY: Backward Elimination starts with ALL 11 variables and
# removes the least significant one at each step.
# Continues until only the best variables remain.
# Guided by Adjusted R², Cp, and BIC.

model_backward <- regsubsets(final_grade ~ age +
                                           internet_speed_mbps +
                                           study_hours_weekly +
                                           login_frequency_weekly +
                                           avg_session_duration_min +
                                           video_watch_time_min +
                                           assignments_submitted +
                                           forum_posts +
                                           quiz_attempts +
                                           avg_quiz_score +
                                           attendance_rate,
                             data   = train_df,
                             nvmax  = 11,
                             method = "backward")

backward_summary <- summary(model_backward)

# Criteria table
backward_df <- data.frame(
  Num_Vars = 1:11,
  Adj_R2   = round(backward_summary$adjr2, 4),
  Cp       = round(backward_summary$cp,    4),
  BIC      = round(backward_summary$bic,   4)
)
print(backward_df)

cat("\nBest by Adjusted R²:", which.max(backward_summary$adjr2), "variables\n")
cat("Best by Cp         :", which.min(backward_summary$cp),    "variables\n")
cat("Best by BIC        :", which.min(backward_summary$bic),   "variables\n")

# Variables in best backward BIC model
bic_back <- which.min(backward_summary$bic)
cat("\nVariables in best Backward BIC model:\n")
print(coef(model_backward, bic_back))
```




```{r stepwise-aic}
# WHY: Stepwise AIC both ADDS and REMOVES variables at each step.
# Uses AIC (Akaike Information Criterion) to decide.
# Lower AIC = better balance of model fit and simplicity.
# This is the most commonly used selection method in practice.

step_model <- stepAIC(full_model,
                      direction = "both",
                      trace     = TRUE)

step_summary <- summary(step_model)
step_summary

cat("\n=== STEPWISE MODEL METRICS ===\n")
cat("Multiple R²  :", round(step_summary$r.squared,     4), "\n")
cat("Adjusted R²  :", round(step_summary$adj.r.squared, 4), "\n")
cat("AIC          :", round(AIC(step_model),             2), "\n")
cat("F-statistic  :", round(step_summary$fstatistic[1],  2), "\n")

# Variables retained
stepwise_vars <- names(coef(step_model))[-1]
cat("\nVariables retained by Stepwise AIC:\n")
print(stepwise_vars)
cat("Number of variables:", length(stepwise_vars), "\n")
```




```{r model-comparison}
# WHY: We compare Full Model vs Stepwise Model to confirm
# which model is the best — lower AIC and comparable Adj R²
# means Stepwise model is preferred (simpler and equally good).

model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model      = c("Full Model (11 vars)",
                 "Stepwise AIC Model"),
  R2         = c(round(summary(full_model)$r.squared,     4),
                 round(step_summary$r.squared,            4)),
  Adj_R2     = c(round(summary(full_model)$adj.r.squared, 4),
                 round(step_summary$adj.r.squared,        4)),
  AIC        = c(round(AIC(full_model),  2),
                 round(AIC(step_model),  2)),
  Num_Vars   = c(11, length(stepwise_vars))
)

print(model_comparison)
cat("\nModel with LOWEST AIC is selected as Final Model\n")
```



```{r final-model}
# WHY: We build the final refined model using only the significant
# variables identified by Stepwise AIC selection.
# A simpler model with fewer variables is easier to interpret
# and less prone to overfitting.

# NOTE: Update variable list based on Chunk 10 Stepwise results!
# The variables below are based on earlier MLR results.
# If Stepwise gives different variables — update accordingly.

final_model <- lm(final_grade ~ avg_quiz_score +
                                study_hours_weekly +
                                assignments_submitted +
                                quiz_attempts +
                                video_watch_time_min,
                  data = train_df)

final_summary <- summary(final_model)
final_summary

cat("\n=== FINAL MODEL METRICS ===\n")
cat("Multiple R²  :", round(final_summary$r.squared,     4), "\n")
cat("Adjusted R²  :", round(final_summary$adj.r.squared, 4), "\n")
cat("AIC          :", round(AIC(final_model),             2), "\n")
cat("F-statistic  :", round(final_summary$fstatistic[1],  2), "\n")

# Final VIF check
cat("\n=== FINAL MODEL VIF ===\n")
print(round(vif(final_model), 4))

# Final model equation
cat("\n=== FINAL MODEL EQUATION ===\n")
coefs <- coef(final_model)
cat("final_grade =", round(coefs[1], 4))
for(i in 2:length(coefs)) {
  cat(" +", round(coefs[i], 4), "*", names(coefs)[i])
}
cat("\n")
```




```{r diagnostic-plots}
# WHY: Diagnostic plots verify MLR assumptions are satisfied:
# Plot 1: Residuals vs Fitted
#   → Random scatter = Linearity + Homoscedasticity satisfied
# Plot 2: Normal Q-Q Plot
#   → Points on diagonal = Normality of residuals satisfied
# Plot 3: Residuals vs Run Order
#   → No trend/pattern = Independence of residuals satisfied

par(mfrow = c(1,3))

# Plot 1: Residuals vs Fitted
plot(final_model$fitted.values,
     final_model$residuals,
     main = "Residuals vs Fitted",
     xlab = "Fitted Values",
     ylab = "Residuals",
     pch  = 20, col = "steelblue", cex = 0.3)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)
# Good sign: dots randomly scattered around zero line

# Plot 2: Normal Q-Q Plot
qqnorm(final_model$residuals,
       main = "Normal Q-Q Plot",
       pch  = 20, col = "steelblue", cex = 0.3)
qqline(final_model$residuals,
       col = "red", lwd = 2)
# Good sign: dots follow diagonal line closely

# Plot 3: Residuals vs Run Order
plot(seq_along(final_model$residuals),
     final_model$residuals,
     main = "Residuals vs Run Order",
     xlab = "Run Order",
     ylab = "Residuals",
     pch  = 20, col = "darkgreen", cex = 0.3)
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lwd = 2)
# Good sign: no pattern, random scatter around zero

par(mfrow = c(1,1))
```




```{r model-evaluation}
# WHY: We evaluate the final model on the TEST dataset (20%)
# that was NOT used for training.
# This checks if the model generalizes well to new, unseen data.
# Metrics used:
# R²   → How much variation is explained (higher = better)
# RMSE → Average prediction error (lower = better)
# MAE  → Average absolute error (lower = better)

# Predict final_grade using test data
test_predictions <- predict(final_model, newdata = test_df)

# Calculate evaluation metrics
test_actual <- test_df$final_grade

# R² on test data
SS_res  <- sum((test_actual - test_predictions)^2)
SS_tot  <- sum((test_actual - mean(test_actual))^2)
test_r2 <- 1 - (SS_res / SS_tot)

# RMSE and MAE
test_rmse <- rmse(test_actual, test_predictions)
test_mae  <- mae(test_actual,  test_predictions)

# Train metrics for comparison
train_predictions <- predict(final_model, newdata = train_df)
train_actual      <- train_df$final_grade

SS_res_train  <- sum((train_actual - train_predictions)^2)
SS_tot_train  <- sum((train_actual - mean(train_actual))^2)
train_r2      <- 1 - (SS_res_train / SS_tot_train)
train_rmse    <- rmse(train_actual, train_predictions)
train_mae     <- mae(train_actual,  train_predictions)

# Performance comparison table
performance_table <- data.frame(
  Metric  = c("R²", "RMSE", "MAE"),
  Train   = c(round(train_r2,   4),
              round(train_rmse, 4),
              round(train_mae,  4)),
  Test    = c(round(test_r2,   4),
              round(test_rmse, 4),
              round(test_mae,  4))
)

print(performance_table)

cat("\nConclusion:\n")
cat("If Train R² ≈ Test R² → Model generalizes well (no overfitting)\n")
cat("If RMSE/MAE similar   → Predictions are stable on new data\n")
```



```{r actual-vs-predicted}
# WHY: This scatter plot visually shows how well the model predicts.
# If predicted values closely match actual values,
# the points should fall near the 45-degree diagonal line.
# Points close to diagonal = accurate predictions

plot(test_actual,
     test_predictions,
     main = "Actual vs Predicted — Final Grade (Test Data)",
     xlab = "Actual Final Grade",
     ylab = "Predicted Final Grade",
     pch  = 20, col = "steelblue", cex = 0.3)
abline(a = 0, b = 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)
legend("topleft",
       legend = "Perfect Prediction Line",
       col    = "red", lty = 1, lwd = 2)
```




```{r final-summary}
# Complete summary of all models compared

final_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model    = c("Full Model (11 vars)",
               "Stepwise AIC (Final)"),
  R2       = c(round(summary(full_model)$r.squared,     4),
               round(final_summary$r.squared,           4)),
  Adj_R2   = c(round(summary(full_model)$adj.r.squared, 4),
               round(final_summary$adj.r.squared,       4)),
  AIC      = c(round(AIC(full_model),   2),
               round(AIC(final_model),  2)),
  Test_R2  = c("—", round(test_r2,   4)),
  Test_RMSE= c("—", round(test_rmse, 4)),
  Num_Vars = c(11, length(coef(final_model)) - 1)
)

print(final_comparison)

cat("\n✅ Final Model selected based on:\n")
cat("  - Lowest AIC\n")
cat("  - Comparable Adjusted R²\n")
cat("  - Good Test R² (no overfitting)\n")
cat("  - All VIF values ≈ 1.0 (no multicollinearity)\n")
cat("  - All diagnostic plots satisfied\n")
```
